root_cause.text: `struct virtnet_info` placed `rss_trailer` (a struct ending in a flexible array member) immediately before `rss_hash_key_data` without accounting for the trailer’s tail padding, so the RSS key buffer started one byte too late and the key bytes were copied/passed to the device misaligned.
root_cause.evidence: The patch notes that `rss_trailer.hash_key_data` is at offset 83 while `rss_hash_key_data` is at offset 84 due to “1 byte of padding,” and that this makes “the RSS key passed to the device [be] shifted by 1 byte: the last byte is cut off, and instead a (possibly uninitialized) byte is added at the beginning”; the fix replaces the separate members with `TRAILING_OVERLAP()` and adds a `static_assert(offsetof(...rss_trailer.hash_key_data) == offsetof(...rss_hash_key_data))` to ensure alignment.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused RSS configuration fields from virtnet_info.
intent_record.what: The struct virtnet_info definition removes three members: a pointer named rss_hdr, a rss_trailer structure field, and a fixed-size rss_hash_key_data array.
intent_record.how: This eliminates stored per-device RSS configuration buffer/state from virtnet_info, so code using this structure can no longer keep those RSS header, trailer, and hash key values as embedded members.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add RSS configuration storage to `virtnet_info` and enforce its layout with a compile-time offset check.
intent_record.what: The `virtnet_info` struct gained a new `rss_hdr` pointer field and a new trailing-overlap definition named `rss_trailer` containing `hash_key_data` as a flexible-array-backed RSS key buffer. A `static_assert` was added to verify that `rss_trailer.hash_key_data` and `rss_hash_key_data` have the same offset within `virtnet_info`.
intent_record.how: This changes the layout of `virtnet_info` so it can carry RSS configuration header state alongside the RSS hash key storage while preserving the expected memory aliasing/overlap of the flexible-array-style data. The compile-time assertion prevents accidental layout changes that would break access to the RSS key buffer through the trailer definition.

grouping_result.intent: Remove unused RSS configuration fields from virtnet_info.
Add RSS configuration storage to `virtnet_info` and enforce its layout with a compile-time offset check.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is an off-by-one/misalignment issue caused by layout of RSS trailer and key storage in `virtnet_info`. This group only removes unused RSS configuration fields and does not address the struct padding/layout bug or the key buffer alignment.

The change directly concerns the layout of `virtnet_info` and adds a compile-time offset check for RSS configuration storage, which matches the root cause of the RSS key buffer being placed at the wrong offset due to trailer padding.

candidates.rationale: This is the last pre-fix field in struct virtnet_info before the struct was extended with RSS-related storage. The bug stems from the new RSS trailer/key fields being laid out immediately after existing members without accounting for the trailer's tail padding, so this is the relevant pre-fix placement point where the misaligned RSS key buffer would begin.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the last pre-fix member of struct virtnet_info before the RSS-related storage was added. The vulnerability arose when the new rss_trailer and rss_hash_key_data fields were placed immediately after this point without accounting for the trailer's tail padding, causing the RSS key buffer to start one byte too late and be copied/passed misaligned.
